sub_scenario.one_line: municipal records archivist: circulate current hold markings before resolving disputes

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the retention index and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The transfer register review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can answer a standard retrieval request on a short call.
Are calls a normal part of your work?
Yes, when the retention category is obvious.
Someone new shadowed me in the records channel this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the audit requests into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For a zoning-record transfer, I cross-referenced the retention index with the litigation-hold notice and sent the department a hold-marked transfer register.
What did that change?
The team kept the records that could not be destroyed.
I can prepare a routine transfer list without a meeting.
Does writing handle straightforward work?
Yes, the register gives staff what they need.
I archived last cycle's notes on the transfer register and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Hold notices can be updated by counsel after the weekly records meeting.
Can you release a destruction list before then?
I can identify candidates, but I cannot authorize disposal.
A vendor call about the retention index ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the records channel checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the audit requests.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the transfer register records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
At a previous live meeting, a supervisor approved a box purge from an old index, and the records staff later discovered a new hold covering that address range.
Why was the approval unsafe?
The discussion used a category without the current legal notice.
I sketched next week's plan for the audit requests before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the retention index updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
When counsel posts the update, I can distribute a marked register and use a live call only if departments disagree about where a record belongs.
Would that support the audit deadline?
Yes, everyone receives the same current restriction before debate.
I compared two options for the transfer register tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the records channel handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The departments want a decision on the pending zoning boxes before counsel's update arrives. How should I handle it?
